title: eval-harness: add CI hook for prompt-set regression checks and quality gating
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: prevent accidental regressions in prompt sets and gate model changes that impact end-to-end quality. This PR adds a reusable CI hook to the eval-harness which runs configured prompt-set suites against a pinned baseline and the PR candidate, computes a small set of canonical metrics (EM, ROUGE-L, BLEU-lite, embed-similarity, and consistency), and applies per-suite gating thresholds to fail CI when quality drops beyond tolerated deltas. The hook is designed to be lightweight in CI (sampled evaluation, caching of baseline results) and configurable via eval-config.yaml. Concrete changes: 1) new GH Action workflow .github/workflows/eval-prompt-regression.yml that runs the hook on PRs touching prompts/ or eval-harness/; 2) eval-harness/ci/hooks/prompt_regression_hook.py - entrypoint that loads prompt sets, runs runner, computes metrics, diffs to baseline and emits artifacts; 3) metrics adapters integration (eval-harness/metrics/adapter.py) to surface embedding-drift and aggregated deltas; 4) small test suite additions under eval-harness/tests/ci to exercise local dry-run and override flags; 5) docs update in redwood-docs/docs/eval/ci-gates.md. Checklist: - [x] Add GH Action workflow and job matrix - [x] Implement hook with caching and baseline lookup - [x] Integrate metric adapters and delta logic - [x] Add unit/integration tests (local sample) - [x] Add docs and usage examples - [x] Add PR comment artifact summarizer (uploads a brief table) Testing and validation: ran unit tests and integration eval in CI; first integration run failed due to ephemeral infra timeout and was auto-rerun; subsequent run passed and produced summary artifacts uploaded to the PR. Rollout: this hook is opt-in by default via eval-config.yaml and will be enabled progressively for critical prompt suites. Maintainers may override gating for emergency merges with the --allow-failure-by-maintainer flag (audit log recorded).

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice end-to-end design. Two asks before approving: (1) make thresholds configurable per-suite (not just global), and (2) ensure the baseline cache TTL is configurable. Can you add unit tests for the threshold logic?

Asha Patel: Thanks -- good catches. Updated eval-config.yaml to support per-suite thresholds and added TTL config for baseline cache. Added unit tests for delta logic in eval-harness/tests/ci/test_prompt_regression_hook.py. PTAL.
Jesse Lin: Safety question: what prevents CI from being flaky and blocking merges? Suggest adding automatic soft-fail on infra timeout with a rerun attempt and clear metadata in the PR comment.
Asha Patel: Added automatic single-rerun on known infra transient errors and improved comment to mark rerun events. Also added an explicit --allow-failure-by-maintainer flag documented in the docs.
Priya Kapoor: LGTm after the threshold config and rerun logic. Please squash commits and include a concise release note.
checks_summary: integration-eval: failed (first run) - infra timeout on runner, auto-rerun triggered; rerun: pass
artifact-upload: pass - summary JSON + HTML table uploaded to PR comment
release_notes: Add opt-in CI hook for eval-harness that gates PRs on prompt-set regressions using configurable per-suite thresholds. Hook is opt-in and can be overridden by maintainers for emergency merges.
notes_for_maintainers: This hook is opt-in via eval-config.yaml. To enable for a given prompt suite, add entry under eval_config.ci_gates and set enabled: true. Maintainers can bypass gating with --allow-failure-by-maintainer; bypass events are logged to audit trail.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: CI could increase PR latency for large suites. Mitigation: sampling, cached baselines, job matrix limits, and opt-in rollout. We included a single auto-rerun on infra timeout to reduce flakes.
testing_instructions: Locally run: python eval-harness/ci/hooks/prompt_regression_hook.py --suite examples/basic_prompts --baseline ref:v1 --dry-run. Example GH Action available at .github/workflows/eval-prompt-regression.yml
